entities.summary:
United Airlines Flight 93 was a passenger flight hijacked by al-Qaeda terrorists on September 11, 2001, as part of the 9/11 attacks. The flight, en route from Newark International Airport in New Jersey to San Francisco International Airport in California, was diverted and intentionally crashed into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all 40 passengers and crew members aboard.

The hijacking was orchestrated by four al-Qaeda terrorists, led by Ziad Jarrah, who had boarded the flight in Newark. The passengers, learning of the other hijacked planes and the attacks on the World Trade Center, fought back against the hijackers, and the plane crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, at 10:03 a.m. EDT.

The impact of the plane and the subsequent fires killed everyone on board, and the crash site became a makeshift memorial to the victims. The flight's heroic passengers, who fought back against the hijackers, were hailed as heroes, and their actions were seen as a symbol of American resilience in the face of terrorism.

The legacy of United Airlines Flight 93 is one of courage and sacrifice, as the passengers and crew fought to regain control of the plane and prevent further harm. Their actions that day changed the course of history and left a lasting impact on the world.

In the words of President George W. Bush, 'The passengers of United Airlines Flight 93 were heroes who stopped terrorists from carrying out their plans and saved countless lives.'
